structured_output.dek: Nothing today rose above background; the only item worth chasing is an NGC2 architecture headline whose body never arrived.

sections.heading: Nothing moved the thesis today
sections.markdown:
No solicitation language, architecture decision, or award today touched on-platform inference, degraded-mode operation, or disconnected processing. Six items cleared the wire; all six scored background. That is the honest read, not a gap in collection.

The useful signal from a day like this is negative: no new requirement language pushing inference forward, and no new evidence pulling it back to the enterprise either.

sections.heading: The one item to chase
sections.markdown:
A DefenseScoop headline dated 3 August — "Army details NGC2 architecture as prototype phase closes" — came through with no body text. On the title alone this is the highest-value item of the week for this profile: Next Generation Command and Control architecture detail at the close of the prototype phase is exactly where the question of whether third-party inference can plug in gets answered.

I cannot tell you tier assignments, interface mandates, or vendor positioning from a headline. Resolve this by pulling the full article before anything else today.

sections.heading: Anduril's counter-drone footprint, restated not extended
sections.markdown:
The Army's sources-sought notice for a Next Generation Counter-sUAS Missile — under $150K per round, Group 2/3 targets, compatible with the Coyote launcher — confirms in passing that Anduril Industries was picked to provide Lattice for the IBCS-M program. That is a restatement of a prior selection, not new movement, but it is the second Army C2 slot where Lattice sits above the effector layer.

Separately, Anduril Industries appears as a catalogue vendor on the counter-UAS marketplace that Joint Interagency Task Force 401 has contracted a four-year-old software firm to build for $15M. Vendor listing, not architecture. Weak.

One caution on that second item: the vendor CEO's "deployed at the edge as fast as possible" refers to acquisition speed, not inference location. Discount it entirely.

Industry responses on the missile RFI are due 20 August.

sections.heading: Weak counter-signal in the enterprise IT lane
sections.markdown:
The Defense Information Systems Agency is running market research on CommandNet, its plan to pull all 11 combatant commands onto a single agency-managed DODNet architecture by FY28 — roughly 231,000 users at 200 sites. That is centralization, and directionally it cuts against the edge case, but it is back-office IT rather than sensor or C2 architecture. Do not read it as evidence about tactical inference.

The acquisition mechanic is the more transferable part. General Dynamics protested a sole-source task order to Leidos under the $11.5B Defense Enclave Services contract; the protest was dismissed once DISA reopened to market research. A protest converting a sole-source expansion into competition, on a schedule the agency had claimed left no room for one, is a pattern worth remembering the next time a program of record tries to expand an incumbent's scope rather than compete a new capability.
